It is found as a minimum vertex cut between the pumps and every reservoir, reference node, assigned flow and other pump (Menger's theorem, by augmenting paths), tee and wye centres never cut, so a header tee lies whole inside. It holds 23 components and 28 connections; its arrangement is parallel: with the pumps removed it falls into the inlet's side and the outlet's side, each pump from the first to the second.

Duty, from the case's solve: Q_st, the net flow from S into the station, and ΔH_st = EGL(D) − EGL(S). Each pump's head H_i is its EGL rise and each element's head loss an EGL difference, so along a way from S to D the heads less the losses sum to ΔH_st exactly: in parallel H_i − ΔH_st is everything a pump loses on its way (its legs, tee paths, and header pipes it shares with others); in series ΣH_i − ΔH_st is the head across the elements between the pumps (the losses of their pipes and valves, or the head a closed valve holds). Shares: Q_i/Q_st in parallel, not given when the station's flow is zero within the solver's continuity tolerance; H_i/ΣH_i in series.

Group curve Q_group(ΔH): the station solved alone, every element outside it held closed and every assigned flow set aside, with S held at the duty's EGL(S) and D at EGL(S) + ΔH; every element inside follows its own law and status rules as in a solve (pumps on their curves at their speeds, a speed-controlled pump regulating, a pump that is off closed, a pump closed by its rule above its shutoff head, check valves and FCVs by their rules, relief valves by their rule, starting closed as in a solve, branch K by the flow split). Away from the duty the absolute pressures inside are not physical, so no NPSHa and no pressure flags are given along the curve.
A pump that is stopped is closed both ways: a stopped pump passing flow (a rotating throttle) is not modelled, so in series it blocks the line.

Points: 41 rises from 0 to 41.148 m, plus the duty's rise; by default from the lower of 0 and the duty's rise to the largest rise the station can hold with flow (the largest sum of shutoff heads s²H₀(0) along a way from S to D, of the members it passes forward and of those beside a bypass in the parts it passes, a speed-controlled pump's at its maximum speed, a member that is off adding nothing, above which the status rules close the pumps; every member's that is on, an upper bound, where no way through the station's parts passes a member), or the duty's rise if higher. items: Station: the pumps P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6 and everything between them and the rest of the network: the smallest part that meets the rest at exactly two places, its inlet S = reservoir B1 and its outlet D = H5 (run_outlet), and holds no other pump, no reservoir or reference node and no assigned flow. It is found as a minimum vertex cut between the pumps and every reservoir, reference node, assigned flow and other pump (Menger's theorem, by augmenting paths), tee and wye centres never cut, so a header tee lies whole inside. It holds 23 components and 28 connections; its arrangement is parallel: with the pumps removed it falls into the inlet's side and the outlet's side, each pump from the first to the second.

Duty, from the case's solve: Q_st, the net flow from S into the station, and ΔH_st = EGL(D) − EGL(S). Each pump's head H_i is its EGL rise and each element's head loss an EGL difference, so along a way from S to D the heads less the losses sum to ΔH_st exactly: in parallel H_i − ΔH_st is everything a pump loses on its way (its legs, tee paths, and header pipes it shares with others); in series ΣH_i − ΔH_st is the head across the elements between the pumps (the losses of their pipes and valves, or the head a closed valve holds). Shares: Q_i/Q_st in parallel, not given when the station's flow is zero within the solver's continuity tolerance; H_i/ΣH_i in series.

Group curve Q_group(ΔH): the station solved alone, every element outside it held closed and every assigned flow set aside, with S held at the duty's EGL(S) and D at EGL(S) + ΔH; every element inside follows its own law and status rules as in a solve (pumps on their curves at their speeds, a speed-controlled pump regulating, a pump that is off closed, a pump closed by its rule above its shutoff head, check valves and FCVs by their rules, relief valves by their rule, starting closed as in a solve, branch K by the flow split). S and D separate the station from the rest, so the rest sees only the flow through them: where the station has one steady state at a rise, its curve crosses the group's system curve at the duty. Every law inside depends on head differences and flows only, so the curve does not depend on the level held at S: a relief valve's set is a pressure difference, compared with the EGL difference across it less its ports' fixed elevation term, so it is allowed inside; an active PRV or PSV, whose setpoint is a pressure, is not. Away from the duty the absolute pressures inside are not physical, so no NPSHa and no pressure flags are given along the curve.
A pump that is stopped is closed both ways: a stopped pump passing flow (a rotating throttle) is not modelled, so in series it blocks the line.

Points: 41 rises from 0 to 41.148 m, plus the duty's rise; by default from the lower of 0 and the duty's rise to the largest rise the station can hold with flow (the largest sum of shutoff heads s²H₀(0) along a way from S to D, of the members it passes forward and of those beside a bypass in the parts it passes, a speed-controlled pump's at its maximum speed, a member that is off adding nothing, above which the status rules close the pumps; every member's that is on, an upper bound, where no way through the station's parts passes a member), or the duty's rise if higher. The duty's rise is solved first, from the case's solve; then the rises above and below it, each from the converged point next to it toward the duty, so the curve is the branch through the duty; a point that does not converge from there is solved again from the initial state. Where a station has several steady states at a rise, a point is the one its solve reaches from there.

Duty check: at the duty's rise 26.9973 m the station solved alone passes 5.67812 m³/s (the solve: 5.67812 m³/s), and every pump its solved flow, each within 0.5 % or 1e-6 m³/s: the group curve passes through the duty.

No standard defines a pump group's curves, and tools differ: Fathom holds a split (equal, or the solved one), WaterCAD reads the losses along a representative pump, Pipe Flow Expert swaps in one equivalent pump. This one needs no split: it is the header construction (each pump's curve less its own losses on its way to the header, capacities added at equal head) carried out by solves, which also count the station's header fittings and pipes. The catalogue composite curve (flows added at equal flange head) is not drawn: it does not meet the system at the duty.

items: Station: the pumps P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6 and everything between them and the rest of the network: the smallest part that meets the rest at exactly two places, its inlet S = reservoir B1 and its outlet D = H5 (run_outlet), and holds no other pump, no reservoir or reference node and no assigned flow. It is found as a minimum vertex cut between the pumps and every reservoir, reference node, assigned flow and other pump (Menger's theorem, by augmenting paths), tee and wye centres never cut, so a header tee lies whole inside. It holds 23 components and 28 connections; its arrangement is parallel: with the pumps removed it falls into the inlet's side and the outlet's side, each pump from the first to the second.

Duty, from the case's solve: Q_st, the net flow from S into the station, and ΔH_st = EGL(D) − EGL(S). Each pump's head H_i is its EGL rise and each element's head loss an EGL difference, so along a way from S to D the heads less the losses sum to ΔH_st exactly: in parallel H_i − ΔH_st is everything a pump loses on its way (its legs, tee paths, and header pipes it shares with others); in series ΣH_i − ΔH_st is the head across the elements between the pumps (the losses of their pipes and valves, or the head a closed valve holds). Shares: Q_i/Q_st in parallel, not given when the station's flow is zero within the solver's continuity tolerance; H_i/ΣH_i in series.

Group system curve H_sys(Q): the rest of the network with the station's flow Q forced from S to D: every element inside the station held closed and one virtual link from S to D carrying Q (a fixed flow: a demand at S, a supply at D), every element outside on its own law and status rules as in a solve (other pumps running, a speed-controlled pump regulating, valves by their rules, branch K by the flow split). Its value is EGL(D) − EGL(S), the rise the rest of the network needs at Q: each pump's system curve with the whole station in place of one pump, by the same code, so for a station of one pump between its own suction and discharge it is that pump's system curve. S and D separate the station from the rest, so the curve depends neither on the pumps' statuses nor on how they share the flow, and an active PRV or PSV inside the station does not matter to it; where the rest has one steady state at a flow, it crosses the group curve at the duty. No NPSHa is given along it, as none is along the group curve: the station is read at its ports, and each pump's NPSHa at the duty is in its own results.
A pump that is stopped is closed both ways: a stopped pump passing flow (a rotating throttle) is not modelled, so in series it blocks the line.

Points: 41 flows from 0 to 2.41023 m³/s, plus the duty's flow; flowMin by default the lower of 0 and the duty's flow, flowMax by default 1.2 × the largest of the duty's flow and the group curve's flows. The duty's flow is solved first, from the case's solve; then the flows are solved as each pump's system curve is: in flow order from the network's initial state, each from the last converged point, a point that does not converge solved again from the initial state, and one without a rise solved again from it with the control valves open. A flow beyond what every way from D back to S can pass (a cut of FCVs at their setpoints and one-way elements against the flow, with the assigned flows), or below the least flow the assigned flows need through the station, has no steady state and is not solved again (Ford and Fulkerson's max-flow min-cut theorem, Gale's condition). A point without a rise says why, as each pump's system curve does.

System duty check: the rest of the network with the station's flow 0.946353 m³/s forced from S to D leaves the rise undetermined at this flow (the rise across the station is undetermined: at this flow FCV 'F1' passes exactly its setpoint flow, so the valve could also hold it throttled, with any rise across the station at or above 20.3079 m (with the valve fully open), and no reservoir or reference node fixes the pressure between the valve and the station): any rise at or above 20.3079 m holds there, and the solve's rise 31.9397 m is one of them, within 0.5 % or 0.01 m: the group system curve passes through the duty on its vertical part.

No standard defines a pump group's system curve, and tools differ: Fathom holds a split (equal, or the solved one), WaterCAD takes the losses along a representative pump, Pipe Flow Expert swaps in one equivalent pump. This one needs no split: at S and D the rest of the network sees only the station's flow.
Method version 1.6.2: every point is a solve by its laws and rules; the station and the group system curve are defined here, not in the solve.
references: Ford, L. R., and D. R. Fulkerson, Flows in Networks, Princeton University Press, 1962 (augmenting paths; Menger's theorem on vertex cuts).
Ford, L. R., and D. R. Fulkerson, "Maximal flow through a network", Canadian Journal of Mathematics 8, 1956, 399-404 (max-flow min-cut).
Gale, D., "A theorem on flows in networks", Pacific Journal of Mathematics 7(2), 1957, 1073-1082 (fixed supplies and demands).
Keiser, B., "Know Your Pump & System Curves – Part 3", Datacor (Fathom), 2021: the composite curve does not cross the system curve at each pump's flow.
KSB, Centrifugal Pump Lexicon, "Parallel operation" and "Series operation".
